Subject: Arkwell discovery — follow-ups + topology questions

Hi Laura,

Thanks again for the call this morning — really helpful to see Redwood's serving approach. Quick recap from our side and a few follow-ups so the team can evaluate fit: we captured the raw notes and attached our security questionnaire (we filled what we could).

Pain points / goals:
- Response latency spikes during peak trading windows are causing a poor UX for customers; we need consistent p95 below ~120ms for single-turn lookups and <200ms for short multi-turn sessions.
- Peak throughput estimate: 150–300 qps for the first region (US-East), with burst to ~600 qps for short windows.
- Model mix: heavy use of a ~70B LLM for core reasoning + smaller 2–3B model for candidate generation/reranking. We need low-latency reranking to keep end-to-end <200ms.
- Data controls: PHI/financial PII in prompts — SOC2 + VPC private deployment required; also strong audit logs and KMS integration.

Technical asks we discussed / need clarified:
1) Rough mapping of p95/p99 latency to hardware choices (A100 vs H100) and per-GPU concurrency for our model mix.
2) Example topology for a staged rollout (hosted API -> dedicated reserved -> private VPC), including how real-time fallback would look.
3) Recommendations on quantization/serving variants so we preserve quality on the 70B model while improving throughput.
4) A short POC plan (2–4 weeks) and a ballpark cost for a dedicated pilot.

Attached: Arkwell_Security_Questionnaire_v1.pdf (filled where possible). We'll follow up with the legal team on redlines after we have an estimate.

Would you and Marcus be able to put together a short topology sketch + mutual action plan by EOD Wednesday? Grace mentioned she can help centralize the questionnaire responses.

Thanks — Sanjay

--
Sanjay Rao

Hi Sanjay / Elena —

Great to meet you both today. Below is a concise post-call recap and proposed next steps so we have aligned expectations. I pulled Marcus and Grace into the thread for ownership: Marcus will scope hardware/price options; Grace will take point on the security questionnaire.

Call recap (short):
- Primary objective: predictable production inference for latency-sensitive flows (p95 target ~120ms, p99 target should be managed with graceful degradation / smaller model fallback).
- Traffic profile: steady baseline ~150 qps, expected growth to 300 qps, short bursts to ~600 qps.
- Data/security: PHI/PII requires Private deployment (VPC) or Dedicated with strict routing; SOC2 evidence and KMS required.
- Model: single large base (~70B) + lightweight reranker; need to preserve answer quality when using quantized variants.

Recommended topology options (summary):
1) Hosted + Dedicated fallback (shortest time-to-value)
   - Hosted API for initial rollout (quick onboarding), with traffic routed to Dedicated reserved capacity for production-critical paths.
   - Benefits: fastest POC start, easy telemetry.
2) Private VPC deployment (target for PHI workloads)
   - Private control plane, customer-managed networking, KMS/HSM integration, and audit logs.
   - Recommended once legal / procurement sign the contract.
3) Multi-variant routing for graceful degradation
   - Primary: quantized 70B (int8/ggml-friendly) on H100 for most requests.
   - Fallback: smaller 4B reranker or cached responses for hard p99 events.

Latency and throughput mapping (initial ballpark):
- H100 (4x 80GB shards) serving quantized 70B: expect p95 in the 80–140ms range at low concurrency (safe p95 = ~120ms) depending on prompt length and KV cache hit rate.
- A100 (80GB) pool: slightly higher latency at similar concurrency; good for cost-sensitive steady loads.
- Reranker 2–4B on a single 80GB card: sub-25ms p95.
- Batching strategy: continuous batching for non-interactive flows; strictly limited batching for UX-sensitive endpoints.

Quality vs quantization guidance:
- Start with 8-bit quantized variant for baseline; run a small eval suite (we can provide a Redwood-verified quality delta report).
- Keep an unquantized reference model in the pool for regression checks and high-value requests.

POC / mutual action plan (timeline):
- Wed (EOD): Marcus sends hardware + pilot pricing options (Marcus: action).
- Thu: Grace uploads completed security questionnaire and we confirm any evidence gaps (Grace: action).
- Next week: technical deep-dive with infra (60–90 minutes) — suggested time slots Wed/Thu 10–2 PT. We'll use that session to align exact SLOs and deployment scaffold.
- 2–4 week pilot: initial hosted/Dedicated pilot, then migrate to Private VPC if required by your compliance team.

Attachments: I've uploaded a draft mutual action plan and marked the key checkpoints. See attached: MUTUAL_ACTION_PLAN_arkwell.xlsx (outline + owners).

Links: HubSpot record + drive folder are attached in case you want to forward materials to legal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/company/arkwell | https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3C_arkwell-poc

Marcus — can you circulate 2 hardware/price options (fast pilot on Hosted/Dedicated + Private VPC sizing) by EOD Wednesday? Grace — once you have the questionnaire complete, add it to the Drive folder and ping Sanjay's legal contact.

If that all sounds right I'll go ahead and schedule the technical deep-dive next week — please reply with availability.

Best,

Laura Bennett
